title: Effects of prone position in spontaneous breathing tetraplegic patients suffering by respiratory limitations
summary: Patients with high spinal cord injuries often suffer from respiratory impairments due to their paralysis. This is caused by the reduced function of the respiratory muscles that comes with the paralysis. In patients with acute respiratory stress syndrome, it has already been shown that placing the patient in the prone position improves breathing, particularly gas exchange. A similar effect is hoped for in patients with high spinal cord injuries, but reliable scientific evidence is still lacking. This study will use existing patient data to investigate the possible benefits of the prone position in patients with high spinal cord injuries. For this purpose, the data of patients with high spinal cord injuries who were treated at Heidelberg University Hospital between July 2017 and February 2025 will be screened, and patients who were placed in the prone position will be analyzed in more detail. As part of this analysis, the effects of the prone position on respiratory function and the need for ventilation will be further investigated.

interventions.name:
one-armed
Changes in patients before, during and after prone positioning with regard to oxygenation, circulatory situation and medication requirements as well as the need for intubation

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Tetraplegic patients with respiratory impairment during the study period from July 10, 2017, to February 28, 2025, were placed in the prone position.
The following criteria must be met:
- Diagnosis of tetraplegia
- Respiratory problems
- Age >18 years
- Intensive care unit (ICU)/IMC stay
Exclusion criteria:
-	Non-Compliance to the including criteria’s
